# Readiness Checklist: Tag Compliance and Ownership

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review focused on four dimensions before `/speckit-tasks`: P1/P2
tier completeness, testability of every acceptance criterion, absence of out-of-scope leakage
(notifications, remediation execution, non-AWS AI runtimes), and cross-spec contract consistency
(connector interface, findings lifecycle, SDA grouping, agent tool surface).
**Created**: 2026-08-25
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature
context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark
an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements
quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## P1/P2 Tier Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is every P1 functional requirement traceable to a P1 user story's acceptance scenario, with no P1 requirement resting only on a P2 story's scenario? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK002 Are FR-013/FR-013a's parent/child resolution and FR-017's scan-completion gating specified as P1 even though they are prerequisites the P2 stories (S22, S23a) also depend on, so dropping P2 doesn't retroactively strand a P1 requirement's own preconditions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK003 Does the spec state explicitly, for each of the three P2 stories (US6/US7/US8), what P1 capability remains fully demonstrable if that story is dropped — not just that it "doesn't block" P1? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 6-8 "Why this priority"]
- [ ] CHK004 Is SC-005 (fallback-chain success) correctly identified as the one success criterion that depends on P2 completion, with no other SC silently assuming P2 exists? [Consistency, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the P2-only functional requirements (FR-011, FR-012, FR-024–FR-028) each tagged **[P2]** individually, rather than only at the section-header level, so a partial read of the Functional Requirements list can't mistake one for P1? [Clarity, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK006 Does plan.md's Constitution Check row for Principle VIII name every P1 story and SC that survive if all P2 is dropped, not just assert "P1 deliverable without P2" as a conclusion? [Measurability, Plan §Constitution Check]
- [ ] CHK007 Is there a requirement or explicit assumption covering what happens to P2's `owner_identity_override` and `tenant.owner_identity_pattern` data if P2 is dropped after being partially built (e.g., mid-sprint tier re-scoping), or is this scenario silently unaddressed? [Gap, Edge Case]

## Acceptance Criteria Testability

- [ ] CHK008 Can SC-003 ("exactly match a manual, hand-counted tally") be executed by a reviewer without needing implementation knowledge of how the score is computed — i.e., does the spec define what "compliant" and "top-level resource" mean precisely enough to hand-count independently? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK009 Does SC-004's "100% of resources created through the AWS console" specify how the test verifies attribution succeeded (email match? confidence level? both?), or is "succeeds" left to interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK010 Does SC-005 define what "correctly lower-confidence" means in a checkable way (a specific enum value, or merely "lower than direct"), given `OwnerConfidence` has two non-`high` members? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK011 Is Acceptance Scenario US4.3 ("well-defined... not a divide-by-zero failure") specific enough to be tested without also reading FR-019a, or does a reviewer need to cross-reference two sections to know the exact expected value? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 4 Scenario 3, §FR-019a]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the three finding "kinds" (missing tag, invalid value, non-standard format) each given a distinct, independently testable acceptance scenario, or could two of the three be satisfied by the same test case without the spec noticing? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3 Scenarios 1-3]
- [ ] CHK013 Does Acceptance Scenario US2.4 (SDA overlap refusal) specify what response/signal an admin receives on refusal, in enough detail for a reviewer to write a pass/fail test without consulting the API contract separately? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 2 Scenario 4]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "at least three modifying (write) events" (FR-025) testable as written, or does the spec need to define what counts as a "modifying" event for a reviewer to construct a test fixture independently of the plan's own event-classification decision? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK015 Does the spec's Edge Cases section give each edge case a corresponding acceptance scenario or success criterion it maps to, or are any of the eight edge cases untestable because no scenario actually exercises them? [Traceability, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Out-of-Scope Boundary Integrity

- [ ] CHK016 Does the Out of Scope section's "notifying resource owners" exclusion have a corresponding requirement anywhere confirming findings/ownership data is read-only exposed (no send-email, no webhook, no Slack-post capability implied by any FR)? [Consistency, Spec §Out of Scope, §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK017 Is "remediation execution" scoped precisely enough to distinguish it from FR-010/FR-010a's own state-changing actions (registering/editing an SDA, editing a rule) — i.e., does the spec make clear that governance-configuration writes are in scope while writes against a *scanned* resource are not? [Ambiguity, Spec §Out of Scope, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK018 Does any functional requirement's evidence/audit shape (FR-021, FR-025) risk implying an AI-generated explanation or summary is part of this spec's output, or is "evidence" specified as strictly retrieved/factual (event id, principal, timestamp) with no generative content? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the spec's Dependencies section make explicit that no non-AWS AI/agent SDK or runtime is introduced by this spec, or does the absence of GenAI simply go unstated (a silent absence a reader could mistake for an oversight rather than a deliberate boundary)? [Gap, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the boundary between this spec's "AI-generated suggestions... owned by spec 6" exclusion and FR-028's admin-configured (human-authored) identity-resolution pattern unambiguous — could a reader mistake FR-028's "pattern" for something spec 6 generates rather than something an admin types in? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028, §Out of Scope]
- [ ] CHK021 Does the spec anywhere describe a scenario where a finding, once opened, could be auto-remediated (tag auto-corrected by the platform) rather than only auto-closed on external correction — and if not intentionally, is that absence confirmed rather than merely assumed? [Gap, Spec §FR-016, §Out of Scope]

## Cross-Spec Contract Consistency — Connector Interface

- [ ] CHK022 Does research.md's CloudTrail-sweep decision (R-302) specify that the new `connectors/aws.py` method stays behind the same `Connector`-adjacent boundary FR-054 (spec 001) established, or could a reader conclude a second, parallel AWS-access path is being introduced outside that boundary? [Consistency, Plan/Research §R-302]
- [ ] CHK023 Is it specified whether the CloudTrail sweep reuses the exact same per-scan-unit AWS session spec 002's `Connector.discover()`/`enrich()` already build, or could a reviewer read this spec as establishing a second, independent session-construction path for the same account? [Ambiguity, Plan §Technical Context, Research §R-302]
- [ ] CHK024 Does the spec/plan state which existing `NormalizedResource` field(s) the SDA-matching and validation steps read (i.e., that they consume spec 002's already-normalized `tags`/`resource_type`, not a second, spec-003-specific resource representation)? [Gap, Data-model §resource]

## Cross-Spec Contract Consistency — Findings Lifecycle

- [ ] CHK025 Does the spec's finding lifecycle (open → resolved via FR-016) reconcile explicitly with the `finding_status` enum's third member (`suppressed`), which this spec doesn't use — i.e., is it clear that leaving `suppressed` unused is a deliberate scope boundary rather than a missed requirement? [Consistency, Data-model §finding]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the finding-reopen case specified: if a resolved finding's violation reappears on a later scan (tag removed again after being fixed), does a new finding open, or does the same row reopen — and is this stated anywhere, or left to be inferred from FR-014/FR-016's wording? [Gap, Spec §FR-014, §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK027 Does research.md's R-301 (rule/finding identity across versions) get referenced consistently everywhere the finding lifecycle is described (spec.md's FR-006, data-model.md's `finding` section, quickstart.md's V8), with no section describing a conflicting permanent-pin model? [Consistency, cross-document]

## Cross-Spec Contract Consistency — SDA Grouping

- [ ] CHK028 Is the "No SDA" bucket's relationship to account-level compliance scoring (FR-018) stated explicitly enough that a reader can determine whether unmatched resources count toward the account score, without inferring it only from FR-018's general wording? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018, §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK029 Does the spec specify what happens to a resource's SDA assignment when the SDA itself is later removed/deleted (not just edited) — does it revert to "No SDA," and is that stated, or only implied by `sda_id`'s `ON DELETE SET NULL` in data-model.md with no corresponding spec-level requirement? [Gap, Spec §Requirements, Data-model §resource] [P2 dependency]
- [ ] CHK030 Is SDA membership specified as re-evaluated fully on every scan (a resource could leave one SDA and join another in the same scan, not just move to/from "No SDA"), or does the spec only describe the "No SDA" ↔ "matched" transition explicitly, leaving matched-to-matched reassignment unstated? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-010]

## Cross-Spec Contract Consistency — Agent Tool Surface (spec 6 readiness)

- [ ] CHK031 Does the spec's Dependencies section, or the contract, state that findings/rules/SDA/ownership data is exposed in a shape a future read-only, tenant-scoped agent tool (spec 6, per the playbook's "leveraging spec 3's rules-as-data") can consume without this spec needing to change — or is spec 6 compatibility left entirely unaddressed? [Gap, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK032 Is it specified that a rule's `definition` and an SDA's `tag_values` remain admin-authored, structured data (not natural language) specifically so a future coverage-advisor agent (spec 6, P2) can propose changes to them as structured configuration rather than free text — or does the spec leave the door open to an implementation that stores rules as unstructured text? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK033 Does any requirement in this spec risk requiring a live model call on a path spec 6 will later need to call synchronously (validation, scoring, or attribution) — i.e., is it explicit that findings/scores/ownership are always available as plain retrieved data, never contingent on an agent run completing first? [Consistency, Spec §Requirements, Constitution Principle IV]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify`
  and `/speckit-clarify` — this file is independent of it.
- CHK029 is flagged `[P2 dependency]` because `sda_id`'s existence on `resource` is P1 schema
  (FR-008), but the specific edge case it names (an SDA being deleted, not just edited) has no
  corresponding acceptance scenario in any P1 or P2 story — worth a reviewer's judgment call on
  whether it needs one before `/speckit-tasks`, or is acceptable as an unstated implementation
  detail (data-model.md's `ON DELETE SET NULL` already gives a technically correct default).
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
